18. My issues wise findings on the issues framed on 15.01.2015 are as under:
Issue no. 1 pertains to the plea of jurisdiction.

However, perusal of the record of the case reveals that the defendant company filed an application for deciding the territorial jurisdiction first prior to the commencement of the trial on 15.01.2016.
The said application CS DJ 58498/2016 M/s Jupitor Polytex(India) Pvt. Ltd. Vs.

The ld.

The factual matrix, involved in the present suit, which is within a narrow compass,
has already been discussed hereinabove.

The crux of the matter is that admittedly,
multilayer films were supplied by the plaintiff company to the defendant company vide three invoices i.e. invoice bearing no. 019 dated 27.04.2011 for a sum of Rs.
57,269/-, invoice no. 077 dated 05.07.2011 for a sum of Rs. 1,08,221/- and invoice no.
176 dated 26.09.2011 for a sum of Rs. 2,29,542/-.
It is not in dispute that the total amount of the said invoices comes out to Rs. 3,95,032/-.

As per the case of the plaintiff, the defendant failed to make the payment of the above said bills despite the facts that the goods were not having any defect and the goods of the plaintiff were up to the specifications.

Whereas, on the other hand, the defendant has taken the plea that the goods were defective and the same were suffering from heavy CS DJ 58498/2016 M/s Jupitor Polytex(India) Pvt. Ltd. Vs. M/s Lotus Dairy Products Pvt.

If the cross-examination of PW1 and PW2 is carefully gone through, to my mind, it becomes evidently and apparently clear that nothing has come out during their entire cross-examinations so as to discredit the case of the plaintiff.
As discussed hereinabove, the receipt of the goods vide three invoices dated 27.04.2011, 05.07.2011 and 26.09.2011 stand admitted by the defendant.
The question is as to whether, the defendant has been able to prove that the goods were defective and the same are lying unused in the warehouse of the defendant as is the case of the defendant.
This court has to further consider and see as to whether the defendant has been able to prove that it suffered losses on account of the alleged defective supply of the goods by the plaintiff.
The settled law is that civil matters are decided on the basis of preponderance of probabilities.

The question is as to whether by applying the test of preponderance of probabilities, the defendant has been able to prove the plea of defective goods; the plea of suffering of the losses and the plea that the entire lot of the goods which was the subject matter of the above said three invoices is still lying unused in the warehouse of the defendant.
It has to be seen that as per the own case of the defendant, the plea of defective goods was raised by the defendant for the first time CS DJ 58498/2016 M/s Jupitor Polytex(India) Pvt. Ltd.

DW1, in the cross-examination, has categorically admitted that the defendant received the material in respect of the first invoice dated 27.04.2011 for Rs. 57,269/-.

DW1 has again admitted it to be correct that the goods were again received by the defendant vide invoices dated 05.07.2011 for Rs.
1,08,221/-.
DW1 has admitted it to be correct that the defendant company has consumed the material of supply of first two invoices.
By way of volunteer, DW1 states that after consuming the goods, the defendant came to know about the defects in the material.

The above said cross-examination of DW1, to my mind, falsifies the stand of the defendant to the effect that the entire lot of goods weighing 3452.9 Kg which was the subject matter of the three invoices was lying unused in the warehouse of the defendant.

The abovesaid cross-examination of DW1 does not leave even an iota of doubt in the mind of the court to the effect that the defendant has already consumed the goods which were supplied to it by the plaintiff vide the first two invoices dated 27.04.2011 and 05.07.2011.

The above said cross-examination of DW1, to my mind, is sufficient in itself to bring home the point that the complaint of the defendant was qua the third invoice dated 26.09.2011 only;
that the said complaint was attended by the representative of the plaintiff; that the wastage was well within the norms and that the defendant was getting the required yield upto 400 pouches per Kg of multilayer film.
DW1 again admits it to be correct that the defendant company never got tested the material so supplied by the plaintiff to them from any laboratory or any agency.
As such, I am of the opinion that the defendant has utterly failed to prove the plea of defective goods.
I am also of the opinion that the defendant has failed to prove that it suffered losses on account of the alleged defective supply of the goods.
To my mind, the cross-examination of DW1 is sufficient in itself to demolish the entire stand of the defendant as contained in the written statement.
DW1 once again admits it to be correct that the materials so supplied by the plaintiff to the defendant were used as packaging material for packaging of the milk.
